Relationship: RFI response days vs cost-impact flag
Interpretation: Longer response time shows a moderate positive association with cost impact.

Relationship: RFI response days vs schedule-impact flag
Interpretation: Longer response time shows a modest positive association with schedule impact.

Relationship: RFI response days vs linked-to-change flag
Interpretation: Response time alone has only a weak association with later change linkage.

Relationship: RFI revision count vs response days
Interpretation: More revision activity is moderately associated with longer response cycles.

Relationship: RFI reopen count vs response days
Interpretation: Reopened RFIs are associated with longer response cycles.

Relationship: RFI response quality vs response days
Interpretation: Longer response cycles are associated with lower response-quality ratings in the synthetic data.

Relationship: Change revision count vs approval days
Interpretation: More change revisions are moderately associated with longer approval cycles.

Relationship: Change submitted value vs approval days
Interpretation: Change size has little association with approval cycle in this portfolio.

Relationship: Change linked-to-RFI flag vs approval days
Interpretation: Linked and unlinked changes have essentially the same approval-cycle distribution.

Relationship: Project average RFI response vs average change approval cycle
Interpretation: Projects with slower RFI response also tend to have slower change approval; this is the strongest tested portfolio-level relationship.

Interpretation: The strong monotonic relationship is consistent with the Pearson result.
